User lifecycle (proposed)
super_admin / admin clicks Add ─► enters Name + Email + Role
        │
        ▼
invite row in user_profiles (auth.users not yet present)
        │
        ▼
email magic-link sent to invitee
        │
        ▼
invitee clicks link → auth.users created → handle_new_user() reads
existing user_profile row by email, attaches auth.uid()
        │
        ▼
role is whatever the inviter set (NOT inferred from email shape)

Worked example
A super_admin invites priya@otomatiks.in as staff:

UI form: Name="Priya", Email="priya@otomatiks.in", Role="staff" → tRPC users.invite.
Server inserts row in user_profiles (id placeholder OR keyed by email — open question Q3) with role='staff', status='invited'.
Supabase Auth inviteUserByEmail (admin API) sends magic link.
Priya clicks link → auth.users row created → handle_new_user() trigger:
today: checks email shape → would mark her admin regardless of invite.
target: looks up the pre-existing user_profiles row, attaches auth.uid(), sets status='active'. Falls through to REJECT if no invite row.
Priya lands on /welcome, then /admin or /staff home based on role.
Another example — privilege-escalation block:

Admin opens the role dropdown for another admin user. Dropdown options: staff, parent, admin. super_admin is hidden client-side AND server-side rejects the mutation with FORBIDDEN.
